knowledge.finding: When testing strong-form betting-market efficiency, normalized/no-vig probabilities are the appropriate probability input; regressions using raw inverse odds can be biased toward falsely accepting efficiency.
knowledge.guidance: Keep no-vig normalization as the default live benchmark and historical-calibration basis.

knowledge.finding: Major sports betting markets are generally highly informative and often efficient within transaction costs; statistical biases do not automatically imply profitable bets after vig.
knowledge.guidance: Treat market price as a strong prior, not an opponent to be ignored. Require multiple independent signals before overriding it.

knowledge.finding: Favorite-longshot bias is widespread, but its sign and magnitude vary by sport, market structure, and bookmaker. Longshots often have worse expected returns, but MLB/NHL and some U.S. side markets have historically shown reverse patterns.
knowledge.guidance: Never apply a universal favorite/longshot correction. Use sport/market-specific calibration.

knowledge.finding: Individual bookmakers can fail to incorporate information already present in competitors' odds; aggregated/market-best information can be more informative than a single book.
knowledge.guidance: Preserve line shopping and consensus/sharp benchmarking. Do not treat one book as the truth.

knowledge.finding: Line movement often improves forecast accuracy from opener to close because informed trading/news is incorporated, although specific markets and early-season regimes can retain biases.
knowledge.guidance: Use close/near-close as the strongest market benchmark and track whether Betting Edge recommendations beat it (CLV).

knowledge.finding: Detailed MLB line-movement research finds forecasts mostly reliable but some repeatable intraday movement inefficiencies; newer work extends evidence of negative autocorrelation in moneyline changes across MLB/NFL/NBA/NHL.
knowledge.guidance: Keep movement path, not just opener/closer, where timestamped data exist; test reversal/overreaction patterns in shadow mode.

knowledge.finding: NHL moneyline research has historically documented reverse favorite-longshot behavior, similar to MLB in older literature.
knowledge.guidance: Use as historical prior only; current NHL price bands/movement still need contemporary validation.

knowledge.finding: Compared with NFL/NBA/MLB/soccer, recent peer-reviewed NHL-specific betting research is thinner; historical reverse-FLB findings should not be assumed to hold unchanged in modern multi-book markets.
knowledge.guidance: Our current NHL open-close and movement calibration remains genuinely useful rather than redundant.

knowledge.finding: High-frequency/in-play markets can incorporate major news quickly, but behavioral mispricing around surprise events and near expiry can occur. Efficiency is not constant through time-to-event.
knowledge.guidance: Live bets require a separate model/error margin from pregame; never infer live fair value solely from pregame calibration.

knowledge.finding: For betting decisions, probability calibration is more relevant than raw classification accuracy because EV depends on the quality of probability estimates at quoted prices.
knowledge.guidance: Evaluate models/signals with calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and realized EVâ€”not win percentage alone.

knowledge.finding: A 2004 reexamination corrected commission treatment in earlier NHL work and still found the inefficiency/reverse favorite-longshot result survived the stricter tests.
knowledge.guidance: Confirms old NHL anomaly was not merely a commission-calculation artifact; still requires modern-era validation.

knowledge.finding: A 2011 extension using ten additional NHL seasons continued to study reverse favorite-longshot behavior and reported profitable wagering opportunities in the historical NHL market.
knowledge.guidance: Raises the priority of modern NHL revalidation, especially by price band and book, but does not justify importing old profit thresholds.

knowledge.finding: Research has found home-field pricing biases in nationally prominent NFL games and tested similar effects in NBA and MLB; home advantage is not a stable universal betting edge across sports.
knowledge.guidance: Model home advantage sport- and context-specifically; never use a universal home-team premium.

knowledge.finding: Conventional bookmaker-margin calculations can understate average bettor loss when margins vary by outcome probability; soccer and tennis evidence shows longshots can carry systematically higher effective margins.
knowledge.guidance: Do not assume equal-vig allocation when converting odds to fair probability. Compare multiple de-vig methods and calibrate by sport/book/price.

knowledge.finding: Discrete bookmaker odds grids can mechanically create favorite-longshot bias even without behavioral mispricing.
knowledge.guidance: Treat some apparent bias as market-structure/margin shape rather than true predictive error.

knowledge.finding: In-play prediction-market research finds mispricing can increase following surprising major events, particularly late shocks involving longshots.
knowledge.guidance: Live-event shocks deserve separate recalibration and uncertainty; do not extrapolate pregame fair probabilities mechanically after major state changes.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 sports prediction-market study using 23 million trades reports that calibration changes materially near expiry and that parlays become increasingly overpriced with leg count.
knowledge.guidance: Treat near-expiry/live exchange probabilities and parlays as distinct products; do not assume static calibration through time.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 study on ~90,000 football matches reports that bookmaker-aware odds-only probability transformations can outperform standard multiplicative, Shin, and Power conversions for many books.
knowledge.guidance: Benchmark our current no-vig method against multiple de-vig transforms rather than assuming multiplicative normalization is always best.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 review synthesizes behavioral, informational and structural explanations for favorite-longshot bias and proposes bookmaker hedging as an additional mechanism.
knowledge.guidance: Use FLB as a calibration phenomenon, not evidence of a single bettor-psychology mechanism.

knowledge.finding: NBA betting experiments found model selection based on probability calibration produced much better betting results than selection based on classification accuracy.
knowledge.guidance: Optimize and evaluate Betting Edge probabilities using calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and EVâ€”not pick percentage.

knowledge.finding: Cross-sport work on NFL, NBA and MLB shows home-field betting effects are context dependent rather than universal.
knowledge.guidance: Home advantage belongs inside sport-specific matchup/fair-value models and should not become a generic historical boost.

knowledge.finding: A 2018 doctoral study using NHL closing totals and associated odds found the totals market largely efficient; only one tested heuristic strategy produced a marginal above-average return.
knowledge.guidance: Treat NHL totals as a high-efficiency market by default. Historical total-angle systems need strong current evidence and price verification.

knowledge.finding: NHL efficiency can vary with the information environment and time of season; treating the entire season as homogeneous can hide information effects.
knowledge.guidance: Keep season phase and information regime as calibration variables. Do not pool early-season and mature-season NHL blindly.

knowledge.finding: A 2022 honors thesis using NHL lines/results from 2015-2020 reported an 8.5% ROI when its multivariate probit model was tested on 2020-21.
knowledge.guidance: Useful only as a candidate modeling reference. Do not treat the reported ROI as established until reproduced independently with clean prices and holdout controls.

knowledge.finding: A practitioner analysis of 12,624 NFL player-prop bets across DraftKings, ESPN BET, BetMGM and Pinnacle found Pinnacle the sharpest of the four and found probability-conversion methods that account for favorite-longshot-shaped vig improved accuracy.
knowledge.guidance: Player props should use book-aware vig removal and sharp-book comparison when available. This is a design prior, not a production adjustment.

knowledge.finding: Targeted searches still surface far less peer-reviewed calibration/efficiency literature for NBA/NFL/NHL/MLB player props than for game-level sides, moneylines and totals.
knowledge.guidance: Props require local calibration, greater uncertainty margins, lineup/minutes/role modeling, and stricter price verification. Do not inherit confidence from game markets.

knowledge.finding: Recent sportsbook and league integrity cases demonstrate that low-volume individual player props can be unusually sensitive to private information and anomalous action.
knowledge.guidance: For obscure/low-liquidity props, increase uncertainty and require stronger multi-book confirmation. Treat abnormal market movement as information but also as an integrity-risk flag.

knowledge.finding: A second targeted literature search still did not identify a modern peer-reviewed boxing betting-market efficiency/calibration literature comparable with NFL, NHL, MLB, soccer, tennis or MMA.
knowledge.guidance: Boxing needs its own odds-history calibration. Fight-prediction models and pundit picks cannot substitute for market calibration.

knowledge.finding: Research on COVID-era betting found unusual NBA moneyline inefficiency concentrated in specific underdog ranges, illustrating that structural breaks can temporarily invalidate normal calibration.
knowledge.guidance: Tag unusual eras/rule environments explicitly. Never pool structural-break periods into normal calibration without testing.

knowledge.finding: Recent prediction-market research finds apparent in-play arbitrage/mispricing can be real but fleeting and constrained by order-book depth and execution size.
knowledge.guidance: A theoretical live edge is not sufficient; Betting Edge should distinguish quoted edge from executable edge and consider liquidity/timing where relevant.

knowledge.finding: Levitt showed that sportsbooks need not simply balance equal money on both sides; bookmakers can exploit bettor biases and set prices strategically while managing exposure.
knowledge.guidance: Do not assume sportsbook prices are neutral forecasts plus symmetric vig. Book identity, clientele and shading can matter.
